items.title: datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages
items.raw_text: datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages I was looking at the Firefox network panel today when I noticed that requests to a Datasette table page were triggering an HTTP prefetch to the next page of rows in that table. This was happening because Datasette pages serve an HTTP link header like this: link: <https://latest.datasette.io/fixtures/compound_three_primary_keys?_next=a%2Cd%2Cv>; rel="next" This is bad. A tiny fraction of the visitors to one of those pages will click the "next" link, which means their browser is fetching unnecessary data and the Datasette server is having to render an entire page that then gets thrown away. I dug in and learned that Firefox has an issue that has been open for 24 years about this behavior... And one of the early comments on that issue links to my blog post from 2002 complaining about this feature. I hadn't just forgotten that I had written about it, I had forgotten the feature entirely! Tags: firefox , html , mozilla , datasette

In Liechtenstein is de publieke omroep ingeruild voor goedkopere AI-radio
items.raw_text: Het is bijna als bij zoveel andere radiostations in Europa en in de rest van de wereld: elk uur of halfuur klinkt een deuntje en leest een presentator het radionieuws voor. Zo ook in het kleine Alpenland Liechtenstein. "Elf uur, met nu: het nieuws", klinkt het op Radio Vaterland. Maar de eerste zin van het radiobulletin verraadt het al: "Dit is met kunstmatige intelligentie de stem van Nicky Stettler". De teksten van het radiobulletin zijn volledig door AI geschreven en vervolgens uitgesproken, door gekloonde stemmen van redacteuren. Ook de muziekmix wordt zonder tussenkomst van mensen bepaald. En zo ziet dat eruit: In hoofdstad Vaduz laat initiatiefnemer Daniel Bargetze grappend de radiostudio zien: zijn laptop. "Wij zijn een radiozender zonder studio, alles zit in de cloud." Het AI-model maakt gebruik van artikelen uit zijn krant, Liechtensteiner Vaterland, die dagelijks door tientallen mensen wordt gemaakt. "De basis blijft dus de mens." Maar presentatoren en weermensen zijn niet meer nodig. "In het begin lazen we de teksten nog na, maar inmiddels werkt alles goed genoeg", vervolgt Bargetze. Kleine foutjes blijven, zoals de uitspraak van buitenlandse politici en bands als U2 en Lynyrd Skynyrd. En hoewel de bevolking onderling een dialect van het Duits spreekt, kan het AI-model op dit moment alleen nog het Standaard Duits aan. items.title: MaxxBench – "Nice DeepSWE score. But is it true?"
The Bantu expansion changed Africa. Scientists are still tracing how.
items.raw_text: It’s not easy to extract iron from its ore. But the peoples of the ancient city of Great Zimbabwe—the capital of a thriving kingdom in southern Africa between 1000 to 1700 AD—were masters. At sites near the city’s stone ruins, clusters of iron-smelting furnaces survive today as mounds of rubble. At Mashava, a village 25 miles northwest, fragments bear fingermarks of those who long ago smoothed the structures’ clay interiors. Some of the furnaces were nearly an adult’s arm span in width, with walls thick and strong to contain the heat of more than 2,100° Fahrenheit needed to smelt iron. Unlike other furnaces that required workers to force air into them with bellows, these were designed to suck air in, then out through a chimney, no human labor required. This would have made it significantly easier to produce the iron, which was fashioned into hoes, axes, and arrowheads. Read full article Comments

items.title: British soldier ignored order to pull his SIM card, then got blackmailed
items.raw_text: An Estonian newspaper recently revealed that a British soldier disobeyed a direct order to remove the SIM card from his cellphone before being deployed to a part of Estonia, approximately 90 miles west of the Russian border. As a result of his refusal to engage in this element of operational security (opsec), the soldier, Daniel Barton-Kennedy, had his phone hacked, and nude photos of himself were stolen and used as blackmail against him. Eventually, Barton-Kennedy was court-martialed for disobeying a lawful command, pled guilty, was reduced in rank, and ordered to serve 10 months in detention. Read full article Comments

items.title: Costco members can get $5 off the reimagined Ocarina of Time
items.raw_text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake showcases plenty of modern effects. | Image: Nintendo While some retailers were offering preorder discounts on the remastered Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time , it’s not too late to save if you missed out. Costco members can currently get $5 off the digital version online, bringing the price down to $54.99. Considering an annual Costco membership runs $65 , that discount almost offsets one month of your plan — a prime example of “gamer math.” The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time Where to Buy: $59.99 $54.99 at Costco (digital) My colleague Andrew Webster recently shared his thoughts on Nintendo’s latest Switch 2 exclusive, noting how impressed he was with how much impact a few modern quality-of-life changes had on what is otherwise a classic experience. The updated graphics are as thoughtful as they are beautiful, pairing realistic scenery with puppet-like characters. Perhaps, more importantly, Link can now jump anytime he likes, rather than being limited to specific ledges.

items.title: AI broke the cybersecurity world. What’s next?
items.raw_text: Today, I’m talking with Alex Stamos, chief security officer at Cognition and longtime cybersecurity expert, about what a mess cybersecurity is right now. This episode is part one of a special series looking at AI in real life. I’ve always enjoyed talking to Alex because he’s so direct, and you’re going to hear him say that the multibillion-dollar cybersecurity industry as we’ve known it is essentially overdue to the unrelenting, AI-boosted waves of hacks, breaches, and attacks — and this is only the beginning of how much AI is changing security. Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here . Not a subscriber? You can sign up here . Both private actors and also state actors, like Russia or North Korea, are breaking into systems all over thanks to AI helping them both detect and exploit vulnerabilities all at the same time. It’s got a real frontier feel to it, Alex notes, just like the ’90s, when the whole idea of an always-online world was brand-new. That much disruption means a lot of places where bad guys can get in while everyone else is left scrambling. Alex isn’t a doomer in the long run, but he does think we’re in for a “dark age” while we try to figure out how on earth to adapt to the new era. There’s a lot going on here — we even got all the way to how AI-powered misinformation and slop might be managed on our social networks. items.title: Cybersecurity is eindelijk chefsache
items.raw_text: Cybersec Netherlands 2026: van boardroom tot slagveld Cybersecurity gaat allang niet meer alleen over firewalls, monitoring en compliance. Het betreft ook geopolitieke afhankelijkheden, digitale soevereiniteit , hybride oorlogsvoering, bestuurlijke verantwoordelijkheid en maatschappelijke weerbaarheid. Dat werd tijdens de twee dagen van Cybersec Netherlands 2026 in de Jaarbeurs in Utrecht overduidelijk. Cybersecurity begint nu eindelijk chefsache te worden. Het hoofdpodium van Cybersec Netherlands 2026 (afgelopen 9 en 10 september) liep op de eerste dag vol voor de openingsspeech van Bart Groothuis, Europarlementariër van de VVD. Groothuis heeft een achtergrond in de ict; hij leidde van 2014 tot 2020 bij het Bureau Cyber Security van het ministerie Defensie. In het Europarlement geldt hij als een van de aanjagers van de NIS2-regelgeving. ‘We hebben sinds de Diginotar-affaire vijftien jaar aangekloot, maar dankzij NIS2 is de ceo nu eindelijk aansprakelijk voor cyberbeveiliging. Het heeft jarenlang geduurd, maar cybersecurity begint nu eindelijk chefsache te worden.’ In zijn plenaire lezing stipt hij ook de te grote afhankelijkheid van Amerika aan. De Verenigde Staten bepalen nog altijd in hoge mate de markt voor ai-modellen en chips, stelt hij vast. ‘Er zijn wereldwijd drieduizend ai-modellen waarvan een dertigtal uit de Europese Unie.
